newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MONACO LOOK FOR WIN AGAINST DEPLETED NEWCASTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO LOOK FOR WIN AGAINST DEPLETED NEWCASTLE.

text.p: Newcastle's hopes of winning their first major trophy since 1969 took a knock on Monday when manager Kenny Dalglish said striker Les Ferdinand was likely to miss their UEFA Cup quarter-final first leg against Monaco on Tuesday.

Ferdinand pulled a hamstring in Newcastle's home defeat against Southampton on Saturday, and was expected to be sidelined along with Alan Shearer, recovering from his third groin operation in 10 months.
Ferdinand and Shearer have scored 41 goals between them this season and with Colombian striker Faustino Asprilla missing the match through suspension, Newcastle could struggle to score.
Dalglish does have other options and Newcastle are not exactly reluctant to play attacking soccer with the likes of Frenchman David Ginola and Peter Beardsley easily capable of finding the net.
But there is no doubt that Newcastle's power has been blunted and that will put even more pressure on their notoriously porous defence.
The French League leaders go to St James' Park looking to end almost 20 years of English domination against French teams in European competition.

Coach Jean Tigana watched Newcastle play on Saturday and said on Monday he was quietly confident that Monaco could chalk up their fourth successive away win in the competition. "We are going there to win," he said.

Tigana will rely heavily on his Nigerian ace Victor Ikpeba, scorer of five goals in his last six matches, to lead the Monaco line. He was also likely to play young Thierry Henry alongside Brazilian Anderson.
But Tigana, who has committed his side to attack, might have to play without former Celtic midfielder John Collins who has been suffering with a thigh strain.
While Monaco are looking good in their bid to lift the French title, Newcastle's own championship hopes suffered a setback with their defeat on Saturday.
The competition looks increasingly like their best chance of winning a trophy for the first time since they won the old Inter Cities Fairs Cup, forerunner of the UEFA Cup.
